notes: Five architectures (gru, lstm, bilstm, cnn, dnn) on the SAME feature pipeline (base_v1, ME-126/xy, 252-dim) and the SAME training regime (copied verbatim from gislr.training.json's `shared` block) for a direct apples-to-apples comparison, including dnn -- which has never been measured on this raw 252-dim pipeline before (only on full-543 landmark_interp_v1 or the 922-dim curated pipeline in other notebooks). gru/lstm/bilstm/cnn here are single-final-fit measurements (this track's convention, see sb.recognize.interp's module docstring) for direct comparability with dnn under identical code; they are NOT a substitute for the canonical, registry-tracked, resumable runs from gislr.training.json/gislr.1.models.training.ipynb (TODO §4.3) -- use those for the authoritative leaderboard entries. `cnn`'s `num_layers` overrides to 5 for the same reason gislr.training.json's cnn1d does: it counts dilated conv BLOCKS, not recurrent layers, and 2 gives a crushed 13-frame receptive field (TODO §5.5.1) instead of the intended 125. `dnn` has no hidden_size/num_layers equivalent (it's a memory-free per-frame MLP, not recurrent) -- `hidden_sizes` is its own capacity knob, roughly parameter-matched to the recurrent arms.

cnn.notes: num_layers = dilated conv BLOCKS, not recurrent layers -- 5 blocks gives a 125-frame receptive field (kernel 5, dilations 1,2,4,8,16), matching gislr.training.json's cnn1d fix (TODO §5.5.1).

dnn.notes: sb.recognize.interp.models.LandmarkDNN fed base_v1's flat 252-dim ME-126/xy directly (n_landmarks=126, channels_per_landmark=2, angle_dim=0, relational_dim=0) -- no angle/relational blocks, since base_v1 doesn't compute them. Memory-free: every frame classified independently, video prediction = softmax-averaged over valid frames.
